notes.title: Version 10 Update (to be released in Early 2022)
notes.content:
[h3]Check out the new Boxscore Viewer for Version 10!
[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39858625/09131643efa85ad2993d371ae595dcd76a08f780.png[/img]
Over the last month I have been working hard on a new Boxscore Viewer for V10, and I have to say I have never been so excited about a new feature in a long time.  V10 will be equipped with a Boxscore Viewer search utility that can search for a collection of boxscores that meet detailed criteria.  Here are only a few examples:
[list]
[*]Search for all games where Philadelphia was the winning team
[*]Find boxscores where Philadelphia beat Atlanta and scored more than 5 runs
[*]Find all Atlanta games in July where Freeman hit at least one HR and Morton got the GS and the W
[*]Find all division rival, back and forth, come from behind, walk-off victories
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39858625/c01e47103ef335b285395879e48bc8b86774dd5d.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39858625/f29bb1e24f5565cab2078fab4fe82ad4825cc6b8.png[/img]

This will be a great tool to use when researching the past before playing a game.  For example, when getting ready to play LAD vs SFG you could search for all previous games between these teams.  If Scherzer is starting for LAD, you can also look at all previous games he has started against SFG (all games, home games, or away games) -- or you can look at all previous games where Scherzer was player of the game.  You can even look for games where Buster Posey faced Scherzer and got at least one hit and at one RBI.  There is really no end to the research you can do with this tool.

[b]Another exciting thing about this tool is that it will be available for use during a game![/b]  For example, imagine that during the LAD/SFG game, Scherzer just struck out his 10th batter.  You could use this tool to find out how may times he has done that so far this season, or if he has done it vs SFG this season, or if he has done it at home or away this season, or ..., or..., or...

I hope you are as excited about this tool as I am.  Feel free to post any questions here!

notes.title: Announcing the Final 2021 Season Library
notes.content:
The final 2021 season library is now available for instant install from the Library Management Page.  This library contains the following:

notes.title: Version 10 Update - Game Summaries
notes.content:
Just a quick update on Version 10.  Right now we are working on a new Game Summaries feature.  This new feature generates text-based summaries of each game and will be available everywhere a boxscore is provided.  Like play-by-play, this feature is fully customizable by the user.  You can even create game summary templates that will be used for specific teams.  We are in the early stages right now, but I wanted to share with you a few screenshots.  Over the next few months I will be creating more and more templates that will result in rich variety of summaries.

notes.title: Announcing the 2021 Playoff Library!
notes.content:
This library contains ten 2021 playoff teams, with active rosters containing players that appeared in at least one postseason game.  In addition, the manager profiles for each team contain the actual lineups that were used during the postseason.  These lineups can be loaded directly by clicking on the Profile button when selecting the starting lineups.

It is recommended that the library be played as follows:
[list]
[*] The Postseason Page should be used to generate the playoff schedules.  In addition, the library is installed with the wild card games already on the calendar.  Users should continue to use the Postseason Page to schedule the remainder of the postseason games once the wild card games are completed.
[*] Games are intended to be played or watched manually.  This will allow users to select the exact same starting pitchers and lineups that were used in real-life.  If the game did not happen in real-life, users can allow the computer manager to pick starters and lineups based on manager profile settings, or they can choose them manually
[/list]
A few things to be aware of:
[list]
[*] The starting rotations specified in the team profiles are estimated based on manager preferences in the final weeks of the regular season and during the playoffs.  These are intended to be used only for playoff games that did not take place in real-life.  
[*] The starting rotations in the profiles were specified as 4-man rotations and pitchers located lower in the rotation can be skipped if earlier pitchers are rested.
[*] The Bullpen Usage setting in the manager profiles was set to "Quick to the Pen" to reflect the way starters were used during the real-life postseason.
[*] Playing time limits have been disabled in the library options.
[*] The Shelled Threshold in the Pitcher Fatigue options was set to 5.  This means that starting pitchers will become immediately tired if they give up 5 or more runs.  This was done to better reflect how starters were used during the 2021 postseason.
[*] The Maximum Pitches Before Tired option in the Pitcher Fatigue options was set to 110.  This was done to better reflect how starters were used during the 2021 postseason.
[*] The Reserve Best-In-Pen Factor option in the Pitcher Fatigue option group was set to 20.  This was done to ensure that managers do not "give-up" and try and conserve the best relievers when losing by a wide margin.  
[*] The lineup substitutions settings in the manager profile were configured so the computer manager does not make lineup substitutions.  This ensures that the lineups stored in the profile will be used "as-is". 
[*] Some starting pitchers that did not appear in the postseason were added to the postseason rosters for teams that did not go very far in the postseason.  This was required to ensure that these teams have enough starters if they go deep in the postseason during a replay.
[/list]

notes.title: Version 9.2.3 Released!
notes.content:
The following updates are included in this release:
[list]
[*]Changes made to support the upcoming 2021 season library.
[*]Improvements to the  CM logic used to pick relievers.
[*]Improvements to the CM logic used to determine when to pinch hit for a starter that is not tired.
[*]Improvements to the CM logic used to make defensive replacements.
[*]Improvements to the CM logic used to pick a pinch hitter.
[*]Improvements to the CM logic used to decide when to bring the infield in.
[*]Prior to this update, boxscores viewed at the end of the game (before exiting the game) did not include who won/lost/received a save.  This has been corrected.
[*]Made a few Play by play corrections.
[*]When the "Runner On Second Rule" is enabled, the CM will now often bunt at the start of an extra inning game in which a "zombie" runner is on second.
[*]When the "Runner On Second Rule" is enabled and it is extra innings and no outs, the CM will now often play the defense in at the corners to protect against a bunt.
[*]The CM will now try and save their better relievers when winning or losing by a lot.  This can be controlled by a new option called "Reserve Best-In-Pen Factor" located in the Advanced Pitcher Fatigue Options.  The default is winning or losing by at least 6 runs.
[*]When pinch hitting or pinch running for the DH, the PH/PR is automatically set as the DH after the play.
[*]The CM now takes the "Three Batters Faced" rule into consideration when picking relief pitchers.
[*]Updated the help text for some options.
[*]The as-played and profile rotations available when starting a game, and when playing a game, now list "upcoming starters".  This allows you to know who is expected to pitch in the upcoming days.
[*]Full team names (if provided) are now used in the standings.
[*]When picking the starting lineups, or making lineup changes during a game, the list of upcoming pitchers are now displayed.
[*]When picking the starting lineups, or making lineup changes during a game, the player up next is now highlighted in yellow in the dialog box.
[/list]

notes.title: Version 9.2.2 Has Been Released!
notes.content:
This release contains following bug fixes:

[*]Fixed a bug that sometimes allowed the CM to use the next day's starter in relief.

notes.title: Version 9.2.1 Released
notes.content:
This release contains the following enhancements and bug fixes:
[list]
[*]Improvements made to the algorithm used to select pinch hitters.
[*]Added a new option to set a limit for starting pitcher durability.  The default value is 140 pitches.  This option is only relevant for old-time seasons.  Modern season libraries are very unlikely to have pitchers that reach this limit.  
[*]Added a new mode to the Edit Managers dialog box.  This mode is called Quick Watch and it will set both team managers to Computer and allow you to watch just the next plate appearance. After the plate appearance (or when there is a wild pitch, passed ball, or successful steal) both managers will automatically be set to Human. The hot key for this is q.  Be aware that Quick Watch hands over all decision making for both teams to the Computer Manager for the upcoming plate appearance.  If you want to make managerial decisions during a plate appearance set the manager to human for one or both teams at the start of the plate appearance.  Like all of the Edit Manager options, the hot key will not work unless the Edit Manager dialog box is visible.  
[*]Updated the User Guide by adding a new Quick Tip section on setting team managers during a game. 
[*]Fixed a bug that prevented the catcher's arm rating from impacting a base runner's steal rating.
[/list]

notes.title: Announcing the 1980 Decade All Time Teams Library!
notes.content:
We are happy to announce the addition of the 1980s to our Decade All Time Teams series of libraries.  There are some great teams in this library, including the 1986 New York Mets 108 win season, the Oakland A's 104 game season in 1988, and the Tigers 1984 104 victory effort.  

This library contains 26 teams, one for each franchise that fielded a team during the 1980-1989 decade.  For each franchise, the team with the best record during the 1980-1989 decade was included in this library.  Because there are no real-life transactions associated with an all-time teams library, injuries were enabled to spice things up a bit.

There are several ways to enjoy this library.  Here are just a few ideas:
[list]
[*] Pick your favorite team and replay the season.  Then auto generate the postseason and pick a playoff team to manage through the postseason.
[*] Use the postseason tool to build a tournament consisting of 16 teams.  Pick one of the 16 teams and see if you can pilot them to the finals.  If your team loses, take over the team that beat you and see if you can take them to the final game.  Keep going until you reach the final.
[*] Use the draft tool to release all of the players and then run a draft.  See how your drafted team does in a full season replay, or a tournament.
[/list]
Enjoy!

notes.title: Version 9.1.9 Released
notes.content:
This update consists of the following bug fixes:
[list]

[*]BUGFIX: Fixed an issue with the CM when the three batter rule is in effect.  The issue resulted in the CM sometimes using a pitcher that is not rested enough to have a chance of facing the required two or three batters without getting tired.

notes.title: Version 9.1.8 Released!
notes.content:
This release contains the following new features and bug fixes:

[list]
[*]NEW FEATURE: The postseason page now allows up to 12 rounds.
[*]NEW FEATURE: The postseason page now allows the user to create series with teams that have lost in an earlier round.
[*]NEW FEATURE: It is now possible to fully rest pitchers from the Browse Players Page.  This can be done for selected pitchers or all pitchers in the library.

This provides some variability, and a nice balance between simulating accurate IP/CG numbers and the user's desire to pull starters before they are tired.

[*]BUGFIX: Fixed a bug that takes place when hitting OK in the PH/PR dialog box with nobody selected.
[*]BUGFIX: Fixed an issue where a starting pitcher faces one batter and walks them, and then is not credited for the GS.
[*]BUGFIX: Fixed an issue where a pitcher does not show up in the boxscore if they do not face at least one batter, but they get an out due to a pick off.
[*]BUGFIX: Fixed a bug where the pitcher does not get a BF when a batter reaches on an error. 
[*]BUGFIX: Fixed a bug where the pitcher is incorrectly charged an BF on a pickoff. 
[*]BUGFIX: Corrected a bug where an earned run is charged when a run scores on an error by the catcher trying to throw someone out stealing. 
[/list]

notes.title: Version 9.1.7 Released!
notes.content:
In this release a lot of work was put into improving the lineup generation and lineup substitution algorithms.  This code is used whenever a game is played without using as-played lineups.  For example, when replaying the 2021 season as it unfolds, playing any of the "all decade/great team" libraries, and replaying the standard season libraries with as-played lineups disabled.

The lineup generation and substitution code is quite complex because it has to balance a lot of factors such as the manager profile lineup generation strategy, lineup substitution settings, player usage settings, inactive or injured players, left/right matchups, and more.  With the release of v9.1.7 you should see [b]much better lineup management[/b] when playing without as-played lineups.  Lineups should be more realistic and if playing time limits are enabled, player usage should be more accurate. 

In addition to improved lineup management there are two new manager profile settings, and they can be found in the lineup substitution section of the manager profile.  The first allows you to specify if it is OK for the CM to reorder a user defined lineup when the CM has made substitutions.  This setting is enabled by default.  The second new option allows you to decide if the CM should consider split statistics or combined stats when building a lineup.  The default for this setting is to use splits.

[b]In this release we have also added the ability to export multiple boxscores in one shot. [/b] This feature can be found on the Boxscore Viewer Page.  To export multiple boxscores just click on the Export All button.  This will cause all of the boxscores listed on the left-side of the page to be exported.  The status bar will display the progress of the export and you can cancel the operation using the Cancel button.  NOTE: canceling will stop the export, but any boxscore files that have already been exported will remain.

Here is a list of the bug fixes included in this release:
[list]
[*]Fixed an inconsistency with the display of team names on the Playoff Page.
[*]Fixed an issue with sorting team names when a library contains teams from different years.
[*]Fixed an issue with filtering catchers in the Browse Players Page.
[*]Fixed an issue with navigating through months on the Schedule Page when there is a month that does not contain any scheduled games.
[*]Fixed an issue with the display of fielding percentages in the reports.  
[/list]

Finally, a big thank you to all of the users that have reported issues and made suggestions!  Thanks to this feedback I have a long list of things to work on, and will be rolling them out as the summer progresses.

Enjoy!

notes.title: Version 9.1.6 Has Been Released
notes.content:
Here is a list of the enhancements and bug fixes in 9.1.6:
[list]
[*]Enhancement: Added several more hot keys.  This allows you to do almost anything during a game without the mouse.  In addition, hot keys are now shown in the user interface so it is easy to tell what hot key can be used for an action. 
[*]Enhancement: Added a brand new interface for editing managers during a game.  Starting in 9.1.6, clicking on the HM/CM buttons next to the team names in the line score will bring up the new Edit Managers dialog box.  This dialog box will allow you to quickly select manager options, including watch the game and pausing the game.  All of the options can be accessed via hot keys.  The dialog box can also be accessed via the Menu button or by hitting control+m.
[*]Enhancement: Added the current simulation date on the top-right of the Season Overview Page.
[*]Bug Fix: Fixed the league reports so that team names displayed in the reports are no longer links.
[*]Bug Fix: Fixed a bug causing the player name to be missing on team reports when viewing splits other than combined/left/right.
[*]Bug Fix: Fixed an error when when viewing the game preview dialog for a game with an invalid as-played lineup, or a lineup that will be valid once transactions are executed on that date.
[*]Bug Fix: The Library PBP file option has been fixed so that it no longer skips the first PBP file in the PlayByPlay folder.
[*]Bug Fix: Fixed an issue with the display and sorting of teams when team names and/or cities are entered. 
[/list]

notes.title: Version 9.1.5 Released!
notes.content:
[list]
[*]Enhancement: Improved the logic used to determine when to pinch hit for pitchers that are not tired.  This update has the most impact for old-time seasons in which complete games were more common.  The logic was updated to allow for pinch hitting for non-tired pitchers more often without impacting the number of complete games recorded during the season.  Users should keep in mind that in older seasons, managers were more reluctant to go to the bull pen and this did have an impact on how often a manager would pinch hit for a pitcher that is not tired.  Y[b]ou can always adjust the Bullpen Usage option in the Manger Profiles if you would like the CM to pinch hit for non-tired pitchers more often.[/b]
[*]Enhancement: Added a walk-off win special event.  This is enabled by default and can be enabled/disabled via the Special Events option group.
[*]Enhancement: Changed the daily schedule display so that day of games displayed are from the most recent day with played games instead of the first day with unplayed games.
[*]Enhancement: Add Fld% to fielding reports and player popups. 
[*]Enhancement: Change 'Leaders-Pitching HR' report so that most HR given up are shown instead of fewest.
[*]Bug Fix: Corrected another issue with importing stats from baseball reference and accents.
[*]Bug Fix: Fixed a bug that prevented "popups/tool tips" from displaying when they appear on pages that can scroll.
[*]Bug Fix: OBP and OPS were not calculated correctly on batter leader reports.  This has been fixed.
[*]Bug Fix: Stats shown in lineup in pregame dialog box were incorrect.  This has been fixed.
[*]Bug Fix: Fixed the "All Leagues" version of the Leaders reports. They were not displaying leaders for all leagues.
[*]Bug Fix: With runner on third, the CM does not remove infield after the runner scores on a wild pitch.  This has been fixed.
[*]Bug Fix: In a bunt situation, the CM does not remove corners in after opponent pinch hits for pitcher.  This has been fixed.
[*]Bug Fix: The extended box score now uses the customizable background color option. 
[/list]

notes.title: Version 9.1.4 Released!
notes.content:
The following enhancements and bug fixes are included in this release:
[list]
[*]Enhancement: Pitcher durability is now calculated a bit differently.  The durability displayed for pitchers is now an estimated durability based on the pitcher's real-life performance and the library options.  The estimated durability may be a bit higher or lower than a pitcher's actual durability during a game, causing the pitcher to get tired a bit before their pitch count exceeds their durability, or they stay strong after their pitch count exceeds their durability.  This is more realistic because managers never really know how a pitcher will feel when they take the mound, and also makes managing a bit more fun.
[*]Enhancement: Improvements were made to the CMs strategy for calculating how much capacity they have in the bullpen during a game.  This allows the CM to do a better job of determining how much depth they have in the pen during a game.
[*]Enhancement: improved the logic used to decide when to allow a pitcher to pitch in relief when they are also in the starting rotation.  This is allowed more often now for older seasons.
[*]Enhancement: Reset the 'shelled' option so that starters no longer become immediately fatigued when they give up 6 or more runs.  This option had a negative impact on the accuracy of replays and is not really needed because pitchers naturally become more tired when they are getting shelled and will automatically become tired when they are giving up a lot of runs.  If you still want to use the shelled option you can easily enabled it on your own, but it is not recommended.
[*]Enhancement: Added more detail to the manager.log file related to pitchers and pitcher durability.
[*]Bug Fix: Fixed a bug that was causing the CM to allow pitchers to pitch too long when they were tired.  This bug appeared most often in older seasons.
[*]Bug Fix: Fixed a rare bug that would sometimes allow a pitcher to hit when they should have been pinch hit for.
[*]Bug Fix: Fixed a minor bug bug with the new 'three-batter rule'.
[*]Bug Fix: Fixed a bug that would sometimes enable the out of town scoreboard when it should not be enabled.
[*]Bug Fix: Fixed an out of town scoreboard bug that would autoplay games using auto-generated lineups instead of as-played lineups.
[/list]

Enjoy!

notes.title: Patch 9.1.3 Released
notes.content:
This patch fixes an issue with the Out Of Town Scoreboard and doubleheaders.  Starting with V9.1.3  doubleheader games will not be auto-played on the scoreboard (this would result in teams playing two games at the same time).  Instead, users should fast play the doubleheaders or play them manually if they contain the team the user is managing.

Keep in mind that currently the Out Of Town Scoreboard only supports manually playing one team per scheduled day.  We are working on allowing users to manage more than one team, and hope to released this at some point in the future.

notes.title: Version 9.1.1 Has Been Released!
notes.content:
The following new features and bug fixes are included in this release:
[list]
[*] New Feature - We have added an 'Out Of Town Scoreboard' to the game!  This feature is disabled by default and can be enabled via the In-Game Options Group.  If enabled, when you are playing a manual game all other games on that day will be played simultaneously and the 'Out Of Town Scoreboard' will be displayed at the bottom of the Play Ball Page.  The out of town games will progress as your game is progressing.  When an out of town game has completed you can click on the word 'Final' in the Out Of Town Scoreboard to view that game's boxscore. NOTE: [b]this option only works if you are manually playing the games for just one team.[/b]  In addition, it can only be disabled when you are not currently playing a manual game.
[*] New Feature - We have added the ability to edit the font size for all of the user interface screens.  In addition, font sizes can be configured separately for the Play Ball Page, giving you the ability to fine tune the Play Ball Page for your resolution.  Default font sizes are optimized for 1440x900 screen resolution.  Users with higher resolution will want to use a larger font size and users with lower resolution will want to use a smaller font size.  These new options can be found in the new User Interface Option Group.
[*] New Feature - We have added the ability to change the default background color used on most of the user interface screens.  
[*] New Feature - The matchup pane on the Play Ball page now uses the new tri-color team colors for displaying the team name.  This new option can be found in the new User Interface Option Group.
[*] Bug Fix - Fixed a bug that impacted the CM's ability to estimate remaining bullpen capacity when managing reliever usage.
[/list]

notes.title: Version 9.0.9 Released!
notes.content:
Here is a list of the new features and bug fixes in this release:
[list]
[*]Enhancement: several improvements related to rotation and reliever management.
[*]Bug Fix: Fixed an issue with the calculation of the pitcher overuse penalty.
[*]Bug Fix: Fixed an issue with importing real-time stats for players whose name changed since the last import.
[*]Bug Fix: Fixed a bug related to the PBP announcement of postseason totals.
[/list]

notes.title: Version 9.0.8 Has Been Released!
notes.content:
The following updates and bug fixes are in this release:
[list]
[*]New Feature: Year can now include the year in player picture filenames.  For example, the player picture filename: Jimmy_Rollins_phi_2016.jpg will display only for Jimmy Rollins that played for PHI in 2016.  In addition, a third search string has been added to player picture searches.  The first search is first_last_team_year.jpg (most specific), the second is first_last_team.jpg, and the third is first_last.jpg (least specific).   If the first search string fails, the second one is attempted, if the second one fails then the third one is attempted.  The player search strings can be viewed and edited in the Player Pictures Options.  FYI: the team variable in a search string will match on both the team name and the team tag (the three letter team abbreviation).
[*]Bug Fix: Fixed a crash when playing an exhibition game with a team that uses the skip starting rotation method in their manager profile settings.
[*]Bug Fix: Improved the display of games in the daily schedule view on low resolution monitors.  The display of the game box contents will no longer wrap around.  Instead, it will compact, then truncate, and finally switch to a single column of games.
[*]Bug Fix: Fixed the in game fielding positioning dialog box and hot keys so you can now hold the runner when the corner infielders are in, and it is also easier to toggle holding the runners when using hot keys.
[*]Bug Fix: Made another attempt at solving the unnecessary horizontal scroll bar that (on some systems) shows up on the pinch hit and pinch run dialog boxes.
[/list]

notes.title: Version 9.0.7 Released!
notes.content:
This update contains bug fixes and a few enhancements.  Here is a list of the changes in this release:
[list]
[*] New Feature: Added hot keys to the Play Ball Page that allows you to control your infield and outfield positioning with key strokes.  Specifically, you can use control+i to cycle through the different infield/outfield positioning (infield in, corners in, no doubles, and normal infield).  You can also use control+h to toggle between holding and not holding the runner.  NOTE: You must stop holding the runner before you can change your infield/outfield positioning.  In addition, you cannot hold the runner if the infield positioning is set to infield in or corners in.
[*] New Feature: Increased the width of the pinch hit and pinch run dialog boxes to prevent a horizontal scroll bar. 
[*] New Feature: Added a green border around the User Guide button on the Main Menu Page.
[*] BUG FIX: Change the default maximum error rate option to 70 (7%).
[*] BUG FIX: Fixed an issue with the management of relief pitchers. Specifically, when starting pitchers that can also pitch in relief are listed in the starting rotation, they rarely get a chance to pitch in relief.  This is typically not an issue with newer seasons, but in older seasons this has a negative impact on the overall usage of a team's bullpen.  This bug corrects this issue and results in more realistic bullpen usage -- especially in older seasons.
[/list]

notes.title: 2021 Library Update Heads-Up!
notes.content:

For some teams, the import may create new teams rather than using the existing teams in the library. notes.title: Announcing the 1990 Decade All Time Teams Library!
notes.content:
This library contains 30 teams, one for each franchise that fielded a team during the 1990-1999 decade. Because there are no real-life transactions associated with an all-time teams library, injuries were enabled to spice things up a bit.

There are several ways to enjoy this library.  Here are just a few ideas:
[list]

[*] Use the postseason tool to build a tournament consisting of 16 teams.  Pick one of the 16 teams and see if you can pilot them to the finals.  If your team loses, take over the team that beat you and see if you can take them to the final game.  Keep going until you reach the final.

[/list]

notes.title: Version 9 of Digital Diamond Baseball is Now Available!
notes.content:
We hope you are as excited about V9 as we are.  We worked hard to add a lot of cool new features to V9, and most of these fixes were customer requests.  Let us know if you have any questions and thanks for your feedback!
[list]
[*]In V9 we have switched to using pitch count for pitcher fatigue. Pitches thrown for each pitcher are based on real-life pitch counts, which are available for seasons from 1988 through 2020. For seasons earlier than 1988, pitch counts are estimated based on the league average pitches/bals-in-play and the pitcher's statistics (e.g, walks, strikeouts, wild pitches, etc). Pitch counts have also been added to the modified Lahman database and can easily be added to existing libraries using the update import feature.  In play testing, pitch counts, and pitch count based fatigue have been a blast!

[*]Also new in V9 is the ability to have the postseason automatically populated based on the standings. This feature is available for libraries that contain one or two leagues, each with one to four divisions. This new feature has made it much easier to create end of season playoffs!

[*]I am happy to announce that V9 has added automatic tracking of postseason statistics.  In addition, the reporting tool has several ways to produce postseason reports.  Finally, you can also view postseason stats in the player popup, the browser, and the boxscore.

[*]In V9, the PBP got better -- we have added the ability to announce pitch counts (both season counts and current game counts) and added some PBP calls that only appear during the playoffs!

[*]One of the big additions in V9 is the recording of more simulated fielding statistics. In earlier version only errors were recorded. In V9 we now record games, chances, putouts, assists, errors, and fielding percent. And we do this for each position played. These simulated stats are generated based on detailed real-life balls in play statistics. The fielding stats show up in a lot of places in the interface. The first one I want to mention is the player popup where there is a new pane for fielding statistics (it can be expanded and collapsed). As is standard in the player popup, the real life stats are shown in blue and green stats represent simulated stats.  Simulate fielding stats are also available in reports, the player browser, and in the extended box score.

[*]Speaking of fielding stats, another new arrival in V9 is the relay play. In V9, plays at the plate on hard hit  balls to the outfield will often result in a relay throw to the cutoff man.

[*]The career mode supported by Digital Diamond Baseball was updated to include the new simulated fielding stats in the aging algorithm.

[*]The 2020 player library has been released with V9.  In order to support the 2020 season, we have added a few new options.  Specifically, you can now enable the three batters faced rule and the runner on second rule (both of these rules were added for the 2020 season). 

[*]The modified Lahman database used by DDBB contains the 2020 season and includes pitch counts and splits for 2020. 
 
[*]We have added buttons to all option dialog boxes that will allow you to reset the option to its default value, or reset all options on the dialog box to their default values.  This makes it a little less anxiety provoking to experiment with options because you can always go back to the defaults. 

[*]I am a big fan of good pitching, and starting in V9 it will be easier to quantify how good a starting pitcher was in their start.  This is because in V9 each starter will be given a "Game Score" at the end of each game.  If you are not familiar with Game Score you can read more [url=https://www.mlb.com/glossary/advanced-stats/game-score]here[/url].  The bottom line is that it is a single score that "measures a pitcher's performance in any given game started".  There are two ways to calculate Game Score (the James method and the Tango method) and DDBB supports both via an option. In V9, a pitcher's game score will show up in the boxscore, in the pitchers daly stat log, and in a new report that shows the top 20 Game Scores in a season.

[*]The Reports Page got a lot of attention in V9.  One of the many improvements is the new report that shows a list of the player's with the most Player of the Game awards during a season.  In addition, in V9 you can click on a player's name in a report to see the player's popup.  You can also click on dates in a report to see the associated boxscore. 

[*]A new general player ratings report has been added to V9 that contains Lead, Steal, Run, and Bunt ratings for players on a team.  In addition, we have updated the team fielding report to include specific position related ratings such as Range, Arm, and Hold. Finally, we have added the ability to export reports to HTML format.

[*]In V9 there are a lot of improvements to the player popup.  In addition to simulated fielding stats, there is a new tab on the player popup that shows the player's simulated playoff stats.  In addition, in the daily stats tab playoff games/stats are highlighted in blue.  We also added a tab that shows the player's transactions (executed ones shown in red).  Finally, for all players we added a link at the top of the popup that allows you to switch between the pitching and batting versions of the popup ... and if a player played for more than one team, there are links at the top of the popup that let you jump between popups for each of the teams!

[*]Looking for more of a challenge when managing a game?  In V9 there are now options to hide the event and base running probabilities.  Specifically, you can hide the combined player card  and you can hide the lead, steal, and extra base probabilities that are displayed on the field and in the "go for an extra base?" dialog box.

[*]Do you like drafting?  In V9 the logic used by the drafting tool was improved, and it is faster too!

[*]Fast play when manually playing a game now supports playing until a run scores, a runner is in scoring position, or a runner reaches base.

[*]The logic used by the computer manager to manage starters and relievers was improved.

[*]In V9, teams now have a third color!  This color is called the trim color and it is used primarily as a border around the players during a game.

[*]It is now possible to export transactions and opening day rosters to CSV format.

[*]When modifying manager profiles you can now apply the new settings to all teams in a specific league.

[*]Boxscores now mention if the game was a playoff game or part of a double header.

[*]'Quick links' were added at the top of all pages.  These allow you to jump directly to commonly used features. No need to go back to the main menu to get to the page you want.

[*]The brows players page now includes simulated playoff stats and fielding stats.

[*]It is now possible to assign a league average file to all players in a specific league.
[/list]
A big thanks for your support.  Enjoy V9!
